edges.description: Tentative Mendelian randomization association linking genetically predicted circulating GDNF levels to cytokine-mediated susceptibility in lichen simplex chronicus.
Cutaneous type 2 inflammation interacts with and promotes dysregulation of sensory pathways in the skin.
Dysregulated cutaneous sensory pathways generate persistent itching.
Sensory-driven itch provokes repetitive scratching and barrier disruption in a self-perpetuating itch-scratch cycle.
Persistent mechanical scratching induces visible skin changes and reactive plaque formation.
Ongoing barrier damage and inflammation reinforce sensory pathway dysregulation in the itch-scratch cycle.
The hallmark itch-scratch cycle causes substantial sleep disruption.
Reactive epidermal thickening manifests clinically as lichenified plaques.

evidence.snippet: Lichen simplex chronicus frequently persists as an itch-scratch cycle, even when environmental triggers are removed and the underlying disease is treated. For this reason, successful therapy requires attention not only to trigger factors, but also to repair of the damaged barrier layer, reduction in inflammation, and breakup of the itch-scratch cycle.
